title: Geometry - Lesson 10 Assessment: Circumference and Pi
description: Demonstrate mastery of approximating pi and solving circumference problems with diameter or radius.

questions.question: Which line segment is the diameter of a circle?
options: a segment from the center to the circle
a segment across the circle through the center
any curved part of the circle
questions.explanation: The diameter goes across the circle and passes through the center.

questions.question: A circular plate has circumference 62.8 cm and diameter 20 cm. What is C divided by d? Enter the decimal.
A circle with a larger diameter has a larger circumference.
questions.explanation: Since C = pi d, circumference increases as diameter increases.

questions.question: Use pi = 3.14. What is the circumference of a circle with diameter 15 cm? Enter just the number.
A circle has radius 9 ft. Which formula setup correctly finds the circumference?
questions.explanation: When radius is given, use C = 2 pi r.

questions.question: Use pi = 3.14. What is the circumference of a circle with radius 4 m? Enter just the number.
A circle has radius 11 cm. What is its diameter? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Diameter is twice the radius, so d = 2 × 11 = 22 cm.

questions.question: Why is C = pi d equivalent to C = 2 pi r?
questions.correctAnswer: The diameter is twice the radius, so d = 2r. Replacing d in C = pi d gives C = pi(2r), which is the same as C = 2 pi r.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should connect d = 2r to the two circumference formulas.

questions.question: Use pi = 3.14. A wheel has diameter 26 inches. About how far does it travel in one full turn? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: One full turn covers one circumference: C = 3.14 × 26 = 81.64 inches.

questions.question: A measured circle has circumference 43.8 cm and diameter 14 cm, so C divided by d is about 3.13. Explain why this is still a reasonable approximation of pi.
questions.correctAnswer: Real measurements can have small errors from tools or rounding. Since 3.13 is very close to 3.14, the result is reasonable.
questions.explanation: Measurement-based approximations of pi may be slightly different from 3.14 because of rounding and measurement error.
